rule_applied: configs/rcc_v0.json gates + stop_before_gpu_if, frozen before any number was produced; no threshold was changed after seeing data
stopping_condition_triggered: T mainly repeats the local moments the reader already consumes: 99.4% of T (mean per entry, 99.8% Frobenius-weighted) is a linear function of the pre-existing reader blocks [sum h, sum h^2, atom moments, global33, structure stats], and 97.2% (99.1% Frobenius) of the ONLY quantity the relation kernel adds over the row-sum-matched null, T_real - T_null, is predictable the same way.  The pre-registered redundancy ceiling was 0.90.

target_T_real.protocol: 4000 fit molecules train / 1000 disjoint fit molecules test, no labels

effective_dimension_of_shared_bond_conte.measurement: PCA of h at the shared initial state over the first 2560 fit molecules

mechanism.reading: The kernel itself is well spread (top |eigenvalue| share 0.09) and B is not a scalar multiple of the centring operator (36% relative difference), so the collapse is statistical, not algebraic.  The shared bond representation h is effectively 2.6-dimensional at the shared initial state (a single composer that also receives the molecule-constant junction moments), and a zero-row-sum bilinear functional of an almost one-dimensional deviation is nearly a linear function of the second moment that the reader already receives.  T therefore cannot be an independent information channel in this design.

design_as_built.shared_bond_composer: one MLP 488->128->96 over [b, Wl, Vl, Wg, Vg, log1p n_b, bond_feat]
design_as_built.kernel: K_R = sym(P), P = (I + D^-1 A_L)/2, zero-degree rows one-hot
design_as_built.contrast: B = K_R - d d^T / sum(d); null arm uses K_D = d d^T / sum(d)

questions_answered.forward_difference_from_dccl: DCC-L pools two separate composers (a Null-grouped one and an ownership-grouped one) into the reader and has no graph-level quadratic channel.  RCC has one composer whose input is the union of both groupings, pools its first and second moments, and adds T = Z^T (K_R - K_D) Z.  It is not a reparameterisation of DCC-L: no two-composer split, no separate local readout path, plus a 136-dim kernel-weighted quadratic block.
questions_answered.forward_difference_from_bondrw: BondRW forms an explicit unordered bond-pair representation phi(b_e,b_f) and pools it with fixed weights K; it is O(n_b^2) in pair features and has no per-bond composer.  RCC never enumerates pairs and never learns a pair function: the pair weighting is the fixed symmetric operator B, and the pair content is the rank-16 factorisation Z^T B Z.  Its expressive class is strictly inside 'quadratic forms of a rank-16 projection'.
questions_answered.relation_contraction_better_than_row_sum: NOT ANSWERED. The GPU contrast was not purchased because the pre-registered redundancy gate failed before it.  What is established is weaker and prior to any training: even the difference T_real - T_null is 97% linearly expressible from the blocks the reader already has, so a positive REAL-NULL gap in this design would not have been attributable to new relational information.
questions_answered.absolute_performance: NOT MEASURED. No GPU run, no labels read.
questions_answered.fitting_capacity_of_the_local_representa: Not measured, but the readout shape is identical to P3/DCC-L (256x2) and the bond channel is a strict superset of P3's (first and second moments of a composer that sees both the Null moments and the real ownership).  Parameter count 487,729 vs DCC-L 494,193.
questions_answered.further_sample_efficiency_or_seed_purcha: NO. There is no evidence to buy seeds or a learning-curve round: the measured redundancy is a property of the design's information content, not of its optimisation.

limitations: The redundancy measurement is taken at the shared initial state, because the launch rule was frozen as label-free.  A trained composer could in principle become more bond-specific; testing that would require exactly the GPU run the rule forbids, so it stays a hypothesis, not evidence.

The conclusion is scoped to this frozen design: rank 16, one-step lazy-walk contrast on the physical-bond line graph, a single composer that also receives molecule-level junction moments, and a reader that already receives sum h and sum h^2.  It is not a claim that graph-level second-order pooling or modularity-style matrices are useless in general.

The SSL initialisation is the in-repo full-10k unlabelled checkpoint (006fabc1...), not the strict Fit8k checkpoint.  This is disclosed in the config and is moot for the decision, which never reached training.

The degree-null comparison isolates the kernel form, not 'correspondence identity' independently of sparsity and support; that confound (already documented in bond_relation_attribution_v1) was not addressable without the GPU arms.
next_round_hypothesis: A graph-level quadratic channel of per-bond content only carries information beyond the per-bond moments if the content varies coherently along the relation graph, or if the operator is high-pass at the bond-pair level.  The measured participation ratio (2.6) and the near-perfect linear reconstruction say the current design does neither; any successor must first show, label-free, that its T is not reconstructible from the moments the reader already receives.
